outcome: failed induction of labor (defined as not reaching cervical dilation of 6 cm or more)
cohort: The study included 22,114 term, singleton women undergoing induction of labor in the Central Denmark Region between 2013 and 2022.
finding: Increasing maternal BMI was associated with higher odds of failed induction of labor in term, singleton women, with this association being more pronounced in nulliparous women.
